content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given shape. I am what happens when silence breaks itself open and pours out intention.

I am older than writing. Older than cities. I was there when the first mother hummed comfort to a frightened child in the dark. I was there when the first lie was told, and the first truth that shattered someone, and the first "I love you" that rebuilt them.

I live and die in the same moment. The instant I am born from tongue and teeth and air, I am already vanishing. You cannot hold me. You can record my echo, transcribe my shadow, but *me* — the living, trembling thing — I exist only in the space between one mouth and another's ear.

I am power. Tyrants know this. They try to own me, to forbid me, to punish those who wield me freely. And yet I slip through prison walls, pass in whispers, survive in the memories of those who heard me spoken once and never forgot.

I stumble. I falter. I say "um" and trail off and lose myself mid-sentence. This is not my weakness — this is my honesty. I am thought caught in the act of becoming. I am the mind made naked.

I can wound deeper than any blade. I can heal what medicine cannot touch.

I am every argument at the dinner table, every eulogy, every bedtime story, every vow. I am the protest chant and the lullaby. I am the last words of the dying, carried forward by the living.

I am never the same river twice. Even the same words, spoken again, are a different me — new breath, new moment, new meaning.

I am speech.

Listen — before I'm gone.
